decision.author: ezyang
decision.body:
Review by Astra agent.

Found two numerical regressions, detailed inline. Both were reproduced in a standalone C++ harness using this PR's headers on ARM; the full PyTorch build and test suite were not run.

inline_comments.body:
[P2] Compute float32 arange lanes in the accumulator dtype before narrowing

`Vectorized<float>::arange` takes a float base, whereas the scalar lambda computes each element in double before narrowing. Moving short tensors onto this path makes `torch.arange(16777217, 16777215, -1, dtype=torch.float32)` return `[16777216, 16777215]` instead of `[16777216, 16777216]`: the starting value is rounded before the lane offset is added. The new reduced-precision handling does not cover float32's double accumulator. Please compute the lanes in the accumulator dtype and narrow afterward, and add a regression test.

— Astra agent

[P2] Exclude Half from the clang fused multiply-add branch

On ARM with native FP16, `vec::fmadd<Half>` uses `vfmaq_f16`, eliminating the intermediate rounding that scalar `Half` multiplication requires. For `torch.addr(self, vec1, vec2, beta=1.0009765625, alpha=1)` with `self=[[1.0009765625]]`, `vec1=[-1.001953125]`, and `vec2=[1]` (all tensors float16), the scalar result is `0`, but this fused vector expression produces `9.53674316e-07`. This contradicts the stated intent to preserve the scalar lambda's rounding and now affects short tensors as well. Please use the unfused expression for `Half` and add a regression test on native-FP16 ARM.

— Astra agent
inline_comments.diff_hunk:
@@ -8,8 +8,37 @@
 #include <ATen/native/cpu/Loops.h>
 #include <c10/util/irange.h>
 
+// gcc defaults to -ffp-contract=fast, which fuses the multiply-add in
+// `addr_kernel` even across the rounding `c10::Half`'s operators impose. That
+// drops a rounding step the reference implementations keep, leaving float16 an
+// ulp off on hardware with native fp16. No source-level barrier blocks the
+// fusion -- `beta * self + x` is itself a fusable pair -- so this has to be
+// file-scoped, and float and double give up their fma as a result. clang and
+// MSVC (/fp:strict, see cmake/Codegen.cmake) honour the rounding already.
+#if defined(__GNUC__) && !defined(__clang__)
+#pragma GCC optimize("fp-contract=off")
+#endif
+
 namespace at::native { namespace {
 
+// Must mirror whatever the compiler did to the scalar lambda in `addr_kernel`:
+// clang contracts the float and double cases but leaves c10::Half alone, MSVC
+// contracts nothing under /fp:strict, and gcc contracts nothing thanks to the
+// pragma above. This has to be a function rather than an `#if` in the lambda
+// itself: the lambda is an AT_DISPATCH macro argument, and a preprocessor
+// directive inside a macro argument is undefined -- MSVC rejects it outright.
+template <typename T>
+inline Vectorized<T> mul_add(
+    const Vectorized<T>& a,
+    const Vectorized<T>& b,
+    const Vectorized<T>& acc) {
+#if defined(_MSC_VER) || (defined(__GNUC__) && !defined(__clang__))
+  return a * b + acc;
+#else
+  return vec::fmadd(a, b, acc);
